problems.title: Menkalinan (β Aurigae) (13 points).
problems.statement:
Almost half of the stars that we see are either binary or multiple star systems. A well-known example of this is Menkalinan (Beta Aurigae), which was initially thought to be a single star, but today recognised as a binary system comprising two stars that we will refer to as Menkalinan A and B. In the following figure, a spectrum of the system (obtained by the observatory of the Universidad de los Andes, in Bogotá) is shown:

Spectrum of Menkalinan binary system in the region of $H\alpha$. Y-axis is for the relative flux, and X-axis measures wavelengths. Menkalinan A is marked as A in the graph, and Menkalinan B is marked as B.

Answer the following questions using the plot and noting that the wavelength of $H\alpha$ line in the laboratory frame is $656.28\ \mathrm{nm}$. Assume circular orbits, and assume that the binary system as a whole is at rest with respect to the observer.

figures.caption: Spectrum of Menkalinan binary system in the region of Hα. Y-axis is for the relative flux, and X-axis measures wavelengths. Menkalinan A is marked as A in the graph, and Menkalinan B is marked as B.
figures.alt: Plot of relative flux (0–1.2) versus wavelength (about 6525–6605 nm region, ticks 6530–6600). A broad double absorption dip with two minima labelled A (about 6561) and B (about 6565) in red, reaching flux about 0.25–0.35.

parts.statement: In the spectrum, we can see the $H\alpha$ line for each star in the system. Calculate the line-of-sight velocity of each star (km/s) and determine, at the time of this observation, which of the two stars is moving towards us.

The binary system is located $81.1$ light years from Earth and has an orbital period of $3.96$ days. The semi-major axis for Menkalinan B (smaller star) was measured to be $3.35\,milliarcseconds$. If the mass ratio of the two components is $1.026$, find the total mass of the system (in solar masses).
Calculate the individual masses of Menkalinan $A$ and $B$ in solar masses.

Since Menkalinan $A$ and $B$ are main sequence stars, use the relation:

$$\frac{L}{L_\odot} = \left(\frac{M}{M_\odot}\right)^{3.5}$$

to estimate the luminosity of each star (in solar luminosity).
